what: The Retirement Calculator shows how much money you need to retire on the income you want, how much your current savings plan will grow to, and the gap between the two. It also works out how much extra to save each month and the age your savings would run out.
All amounts can be shown in today's money, so you can compare them with prices now. You can pick from about 40 currencies or type your own symbol, and everything runs in your browser.
uses: See the nest egg needed for the yearly income you want.
Check if you are on track
Compare what your plan grows to with the target.
See how much more to save each month to close a gap.
Change the retirement age and watch the numbers move.
Follow your balance year by year after you stop work.
tutorial: Choose it in "Currency". The site guesses it from your browser language; pick "Other" to type a symbol.
Type your "Current age", "Retirement age" and "Plan until age" (for example 90 or 95).
Enter "Savings so far", "You add each month" and how much you raise your saving each year.
Enter the yearly return before and after retiring and the inflation rate.
Enter the yearly income you want in today's money, any pension or other income, and a safe withdrawal rate (3–4% is common).
See the target, what you are on track for, the shortfall or surplus, the extra to save each month and the age your money lasts until.
Switch the chart between today's money and future money, and download the table as CSV.
features: Target = (income − other income) ÷ withdrawal rate, in today's money.
Returns are compounded monthly at a rate that gives the same yearly result as the rate you enter.
Your monthly saving can grow each year, for example with pay rises.
Every amount can be shown in today's money.
After retirement the tool withdraws the income you want each month, rising with inflation, and finds when savings run out.
Shows the level extra monthly amount that would close the gap by your retirement age.
Download the year-by-year table or copy a short summary.

example.title: Worked example: age 35, retiring at 65
example.text: You have 50,000 saved and add 500 a month, raising it 2% a year, with 6% growth and 2.5% inflation. For 40,000 a year at a 4% withdrawal rate you need 1,000,000 in today's money. Your plan reaches about 893,000 in future money, which is about 425,750 in today's money, a shortfall of about 574,250. Saving about 1,236 more each month would close the gap; without it, the money runs out at about age 76.

tips: Use cautious returns: 4–6% before retiring and lower after is a common starting point.
Include any state or workplace pension in today's money to avoid overestimating what you need.
A lower withdrawal rate (3–3.5%) gives a bigger safety margin for a long retirement.
Review the plan every year with your real balance.
Small increases to monthly saving early on make a big difference because of compounding.
problems: I see a dash and a red message
One of the boxes is out of range, for example a retirement age before your current age. Fix the box named in the message.
The extra to save looks very large
The gap is big or there are few years left. Try a later retirement age, a lower income or a higher saving rate.
"Your money lasts until" shows a plus sign
Your savings last past your "Plan until age". Raise that age to see how far they go.
The numbers differ from my pension provider
Providers use their own returns, fees, taxes and annuity rates. This tool uses simple steady growth.
